title: Termination assistance, transition period and in-flight transactions
status_rationale: UNB-TEN-011 requires governed offboarding; UNB-XIN-SAS-007 defines a PartnerExit case including handling of accepted recommendations; daf-landscape documents that some providers end access at termination while prior grant obligations survive. No exit plan or contract exists.
target_answer: On notice of termination, Echelon provides a transition period of up to 12 months at unchanged service levels, a jointly maintained exit plan, cooperation with the successor provider, and a defined treatment for every in-flight item: pending recommendations, approved but unpaid grants, recurring grants, ACH items in process, outstanding checks and open compliance cases are either completed under the sponsor's direction or handed off with full records. The exit plan is tested by a dry-run export and reconciliation at least annually.
intended_practice: Write a standard exit plan template and termination assistance schedule before first contract.
provable: Nothing operational. Only requirement text in the Unbound baseline (unbound@9b38de47) can be shown, and it proves intent, not operation.
customer_statement: Unbound is not yet in production. Its requirements specify governed tenant offboarding and a structured partner exit process that reconciles every fund and in-flight recommendation. This is a design commitment, not an operating control, and has not been independently verified.
external_assurance: None. No SOC 2 report, ISO certification, privacy assessment or other independent assurance exists for any Echelon service as of 2026-11-25.

title: Data return, access windows and deletion certification at exit
status_rationale: UNB-TEN-016 requires an evidence-complete export; UNB-TEN-011 requires evidenced offboarding; daf-landscape notes that some provider terms end access on termination. No contract terms exist.
target_answer: At termination Echelon delivers a final complete export within 10 business days, keeps read-only access open for 90 days, and does not withhold data during a fee dispute. After the customer confirms receipt (or 90 days pass), Echelon deletes the tenant's data by key destruction, lets backups expire on the published cycle, retains only what law requires with the basis stated, and issues an evidence-generated deletion certificate (ANS-RET-007).
intended_practice: Encode exit timelines in the standard agreement; build read-only tenant mode.

title: Wind-down if Echelon fails, is acquired or changes control
status_rationale: Echelon is a newly formed LLC with no published financial statements, funding or insurance (current-state brief). The cross-industry failure catalog in Unbound research identifies vendor insolvency before export as a scenario (XFC-SAS-011) and proposes escrowed export package and schema with read-only continuity; this is a research proposal, not an adopted requirement.
target_answer: Customer continuity does not depend on Echelon surviving. Each sponsor receives scheduled full exports to storage it controls; export schemas and a minimal read-only viewer are escrowed or openly published; Echelon maintains a funded wind-down plan covering at least the contractual transition period; contracts allow termination on change of control and require any acquirer to assume exit obligations. A read-only continuity mode can be operated by a successor using the escrowed materials.
current_practice: Unknown; no wind-down plan, funding reserve or change-of-control terms exist.
intended_practice: Decide whether to offer customer-owned export destinations and a wind-down reserve; draft change-of-control terms.
customer_statement: Echelon is an early-stage company and has not yet established a wind-down plan or reserve. Its intended approach is to make customer continuity independent of Echelon's survival through continuous exports to customer-controlled storage; this is not available today.
external_assurance: None. No SOC 2 report, ISO certification, privacy assessment or other independent assurance exists for any Echelon service as of 2026-11-25.

open_questions: What runway and reserve can Echelon commit to fund an orderly wind-down, and who would execute it if the founder were unavailable?
Would scheduled exports to sponsor-owned storage be accepted by sponsors' security teams?

challenge.customer_intent: Customer wants to survive the vendor's failure without losing data or operations.
challenge.adverse_outcome: Vendor insolvency halts grantmaking and strands records; an acquirer changes terms or shuts the product.
challenge.conventional_control_effectiveness: Escrow and financial-stability reviews rarely ensure continuity; released code without operators and infrastructure is often unusable in practice.
challenge.legally_required: Not legally required of Echelon; bank customers are expected to plan for vendor failure under third-party risk guidance.
challenge.contractually_required: Larger customers request change-of-control termination rights and escrow.
challenge.historical_convention: Software escrow was designed for on-premises software, where the customer could run released code.
challenge.architectural_elimination: If customers always hold a current, complete, documented copy of their data, vendor failure becomes a migration rather than a loss.
challenge.automatic_enforcement: Scheduled exports to customer-owned storage run without human action.
challenge.continuous_evidence: Export manifests delivered daily are continuous evidence of recoverability.
challenge.stronger_alternative: Continuous customer-held exports plus openly published schemas, complemented by contractual change-of-control rights.
challenge.alternative_verifiable: Yes: customers can verify they hold current, reconcilable exports.
challenge.customer_acceptance_likelihood: Uncertain: institutions may still require escrow and financial reviews.
challenge.invalidating_conditions: If exports are not loaded or tested by the customer, recoverability is assumed rather than shown.
challenge.alternative_risks: Customer-held copies increase the customer's security burden.
supporting_arguments: Addresses the actual failure mode (data stranding) directly.
Does not depend on a court or escrow agent acting quickly.
opposing_arguments: Does not give the customer a running system, only data.
A sponsor still needs a successor administrator to operate.

title: Regulatory continuity for the sponsor through exit
status_rationale: UNB-XIN-SAS-007 specifies partner exit with sponsor decision per fund and reconciliation; CNV-PAY-001 makes Unbound a third-party service provider with the sponsor as originator; CNV-PLT-004 sets record retention. No regulatory continuity plan exists.
target_answer: Exit never interrupts the sponsor's legal obligations: acknowledgments and statements for the final period are issued or handed over, Form 990 and Schedule D support is exported for every open year, sanctions and eligibility records are preserved, partner exits follow UNB-XIN-SAS-007 with sponsor discretion preserved per fund, payment rail roles and bank arrangements are unwound in sequence with the ODFI, and Echelon remains contractually available to produce records it still holds for regulator or IRS requests during the post-termination retention period.
intended_practice: Add a regulatory continuity checklist to the exit plan template.

title: Fees and contract terms at exit
status_rationale: No Echelon commercial terms exist. daf-landscape documents public DAF administrator templates with one-year auto-renewal, 60-day nonrenewal notice, termination fees through the end of the termination quarter and liability caps (research/ren-legal-entities-public-msa-contract-portability-audit-2026-11-12.md).
target_answer: Echelon's standard terms carry no exit fee and no charge for standard exports; termination assistance beyond standard exports is priced in a published rate schedule; customers may terminate for convenience on reasonable notice; renewal requires affirmative notice or allows termination at any time after the initial term; confidentiality, data protection, deletion and record-production obligations survive termination; customers have perpetual rights to use exported data and reports.
intended_practice: Draft exit-friendly standard terms; decide the business tradeoff of no termination fee.
customer_statement: Echelon has not yet published commercial terms. Its intended position is no exit or export fees; this is not yet a contractual commitment.
external_assurance: None. No SOC 2 report, ISO certification, privacy assessment or other independent assurance exists for any Echelon service as of 2026-11-25.

open_questions: Can Echelon's economics sustain no-fee exit and termination for convenience while it has few customers?

challenge.customer_intent: Customer wants exit to be economically possible, not only contractually permitted.
challenge.adverse_outcome: Switching costs and fees lock a sponsor into an unsatisfactory vendor.
challenge.conventional_control_effectiveness: Negotiated exit fee caps help but are often offset by auto-renewal and notice traps.
challenge.contractually_required: Exit terms are negotiated case by case.
challenge.historical_convention: Vendors use renewal terms and fees to stabilize revenue.
challenge.architectural_elimination: Making export self-service and continuous removes most of the cost a vendor would otherwise charge for.
challenge.continuous_evidence: Published rate schedule and standard terms are inspectable.
challenge.stronger_alternative: No exit fees supported by low-cost self-service portability.
challenge.customer_acceptance_likelihood: Likely welcomed by customers; investors may object.
challenge.invalidating_conditions: If Echelon needs lock-in revenue to survive, the commitment may be abandoned.
challenge.alternative_risks: Lower revenue predictability for an early-stage company, which itself is a continuity risk for customers.
opposing_arguments: Early-stage revenue instability is itself a customer risk.
Customers may value price stability over exit flexibility.
